title: MCP Client Integration in .NET
description: Connect .NET applications to external MCP servers, dynamically discover tools, and integrate them into Microsoft.Extensions.AI and Semantic Kernel.

data.text: While building MCP servers allows you to expose enterprise tools to external clients, building an MCP Client in .NET allows your own backend AI workflows to dynamically connect to any existing MCP server—such as the official GitHub, PostgreSQL, Brave Search, or filesystem MCP servers. Your .NET application queries the server's tools/list, wraps each discovered tool as an AIFunction in Microsoft.Extensions.AI, and equips your agent with dynamic external capabilities.

data.caption: Bridging MCP Server Tools into Microsoft.Extensions.AI IChatClient

    ChatClient -->|"Model requests tool call"| InvocationDispatcher["Tool Call Invocation"]

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: MCP clients allow .NET systems to consume any standard MCP server dynamically
Manage stdio servers as supervised child processes with redirected I/O streams
Convert discovered tools dynamically into AIFunction instances for Microsoft.Extensions.AI
Decouple AI agent logic from third-party APIs by delegating tool execution to modular MCP servers
Always handle process cancellation and disposal to prevent orphan zombie processes
data.takeaway: By implementing an MCP client, your .NET AI workflows gain instant access to an entire open ecosystem of pre-built tools for GitHub, databases, search, and cloud infrastructure.
